zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is less (or greater) than Y's.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply when a clue mentions a non‑adjacent left/right relationship between two entities.
zebralogic.example: Placing X to the right of Y even though the clue says X is somewhere to the left of Y.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the associate degree holder owns the Toyota Camry"), treat them as the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply when a clue directly links two attribute values with wording like "is", "equals", or "has".
zebralogic.example: Treating "A owns B" as a separate fact instead of linking the person with the car model.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, enforce that exact placement as a hard constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply when a clue states that a particular attribute belongs to house 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.
zebralogic.example: Assigning a value to a house other than the specified house number.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: The solution JSON must be the very last part of the response with no extra characters after it; otherwise the verifier may miss the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply at the very end of the response, just before outputting the JSON.
zebralogic.example: Appending extra commentary after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house, enforce that the attribute is not placed there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply whenever a clue contains wording like "is not in the first house" or "cannot be house 3".
zebralogic.example: Placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B and B = C), propagate the equivalence so all involved attributes are linked.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply after gathering all direct equivalences to deduce indirect links across several attributes.
zebralogic.example: Failing to propagate equivalence across a chain, leaving some attributes unlinked.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling, case, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply when writing the final JSON to ensure each value matches the source text verbatim.
zebralogic.example: Changing the case of an attribute value (e.g., "Bob" to "bob"), causing a mismatch.

zebralogic.title: LimitReasoningLength
zebralogic.principle: Keep reasoning concise enough to stay within the model's token budget; avoid overly verbose explanations that may cause truncation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply throughout the reasoning process, especially for larger puzzles with many clues.
zebralogic.example: Providing an overly long explanation that exceeds token limit, leading to truncation.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacencyConstraint
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is exactly one less (or greater) than Y's.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply for clues containing "directly left of", "directly right of", "next to", or "adjacent to".
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as just "somewhere left of", allowing non‑adjacent placements.

zebralogic.title: ChildRelationshipParsing
zebralogic.principle: When a clue refers to a person as the mother/father of X, interpret it as linking the child attribute to X (i.e., the person’s child is X). This creates an equivalence between the person and the child name, enabling the use of equivalence and adjacency constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains phrases like "mother of X", "father of X", "person whose child is X", or similar relational references to a child name.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "the mother of Timothy" as a separate entity instead of linking it to child=Timothy, missing the adjacency constraint.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the meaning of "between" (exact number of houses separating two entities) with a simple distance measure.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "N houses between X and Y" means there are exactly N houses in the middle, so the distance between X and Y is N+1.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The verifier extracts the last JSON block; any trailing characters prevent detection.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output the JSON as the very last part of the response with no extra characters after it.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the verifier to truncate
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Overly long reasoning can exceed the model's output window, leading to truncation of the final answer.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep explanations concise and stay within the token budget.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model fails to enforce constraints that prohibit certain placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply negative constraints to exclude prohibited house positions during solving.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets to output the required JSON format at the end of the response.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always include the solution JSON at the end of the response.
